text:
maya: Spawning a short thread to align on the "surface-trim" cutover plan. Goal: roll modular slices over 6 months, minimize cross-service fallout.

devin: Love the name. What's the proposed sequence?

maya: High level: 1) classify slices by user-impact and debt bucket, 2) require owners to remediate BLOCKING debt, 3) run chop-and-stabilize canary, 4) phased traffic shifts with memory + latency gates, 5) finalize cut and retire legacy path.

rachel: Define "debt bucket" please. We need concrete categories for automation eligibility.

maya: Draft taxonomy: SAFETY (cross-tenant leaks, auth bugs), CONSISTENCY (race conditions, DB schema drift), OPERABILITY (missing metrics/alerts, poor dashboards), COST (inefficient hot loops), TESTABILITY (no integration tests). Mark SAFETY/CONSISTENCY as BLOCKING.

sam: For each slice we should capture an "automation readiness" boolean: auto-rollbacks, prometheus smoke job present, and a canary dashboard. If not ready, block.

maya: Agreed. Also adding a short "rollback capsule" per row: 2-3 step minimal procedure that oncall can run from the incident page. Example for request-proxy: 1) flip header flag to legacy, 2) scale down new pool, 3) invalidate local caches.

devin: We must include migration windows for consumers. If external integrators can't move within 30 days, escalate to product. Also require a compatibility shim for 60d grace.

rachel: Cost note: only GOLD slices get dedicated nodes during cutover. Everything else uses preemptible/shared. Put a cost ceiling per slice so finance can sign off.

maya: I'll add a preferred_infra and max_monthly_delta column. Also planning a short validation matrix: perf smoke (p95/p99), memory spike test, schema backward-check, tenant isolation chaos.

sam: What's the traffic ramp cadence? We should be conservative for stateful slices. I'd do 0% -> 5% -> 20% -> 60% -> 100% with a manual hold after 20% for 24-72h. Automatic rollback triggers: error_rate > 2x baseline, p95 > 2x baseline, or memory > threshold.
maya: That's the plan. Add a canary hold gating step and require a visible trace sample for any latency spike > baseline.

devin: How are we tracking signoffs? A single source of truth repo?
maya: Yes: docs/operational/surface-trim/matrix.csv (each row: slice, owner_team, fallback_ops, debt_bucket, automation_ready, migration_window, infra, rollback_capsule, est_remed_hours, cost_ceiling). Teams must open a PR and tag @product @eng-sre before the slice is scheduled.

rachel: SRE needs templated alerts + a smoke job snippet. I can author the prometheus rules if someone gives the target metrics to watch.
sam: I’ll draft alert thresholds. Suggest capturing baseline percentiles before any traffic shift; use a 7d rolling baseline.

maya: Action items: 1) maya: publish first-pass matrix CSV and playbook by EOD. 2) teams: review rows and label debt within 4 business days. 3) eng-sre: provide smoke job template + alert CR. 4) product: confirm integration migration windows for any external consumers.

release-bot: Note: schedule created: surface-trim-phase-1 starts in 3 weeks. Please complete signoffs before then.

devin: Two risks to call out: a) shared in-process caches that will need tenant-aware rework, b) long-running migrations that can't be rolled back trivially. We should mark those as high-risk and do pre-cutover dry runs.

maya: I'll flag those rows and require a dry-run milestone. Also adding a short "post-cut KPI" bucket: error budget burn, median latency, cost delta, and feature correctness signals. We'll monitor for 30 days post-cut for each slice.

rachel: Nice. One last ask: include a tiny consumer-facing deprecation note template for product to send to integrators.

maya: Will do. Thanks all 3@devin @rachel @sam. I'll post the PR link when it's live.

sam: :thumbsup:
